text: Write a class that defends its mutable field on the way in and on the way out. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: Defensive(List<String> items) { this.items = ___; }   // copy on the way in
List<String> items() { return ___; }                  // snapshot on the way out
explanation: Verified: `[a]`. Both copies are needed and for the same reason: without the inbound one the caller retains a reference to your state, and without the outbound one you hand it to the next caller. The cost is allocation, which is why Chapter 22's records — immutable by construction — are the cheaper answer whenever the type is genuinely just its data.
